acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Great Cats family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Sabercat, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Pinning Champion archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Heavy forequarters, paired saber canines, short powerful tail, scarred shoulders, and a low spring-loaded stance.
Signature mechanic: Twin-Canine Pin: both sabers plant beside the target and cannot withdraw until the Sabercat resets its forequarters.
battlefieldDuty: Commit both long canines to a ground pin that gives lesser Cats safer approach angles.
constructionDimensions: Streaming wet fur, reflective whiskers, coherent droplets, and visible muscle beneath saturated coat preserve the feline body.
Narrow water wakes follow pounces and territory lanes, with pressure gathering at paws and jaw before release.
counterplay: Dodge inside the leap and punish the planted canines or exposed ribs before withdrawal. Affinity signal: The loaded paw or jaw channel drains after the attack and reveals the ordinary landing or pin window.
forbiddenTreatments: Splash that obscures eye line, claws, or tail direction
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged feline body, flexible spine, retractile claws, whiskered muzzle, mobile ears, and expressive tail.
Species variation remains feline and is communicated by coat pattern, limb proportion, mane, canine length, and hunting posture rather than equipment.
Eye line, tail stillness, shoulder compression, cover disturbance, and landing posture preserve readable attack direction.
telegraph: Its jaws open fully, forepaws widen, and heavy shoulders rise before the leap.
